summary.business: INDO SMC Limited designs and manufactures enclosure boxes for energy meters, HTCT/HTPT/LTCT transformers, LT/HT distribution boxes and panels, FRP grating, junction boxes, feeder pillars and other power distribution and circuit-protection switchgear. The business is organised into three divisions: sheet moulding compound (SMC enclosure boxes, SMC sheet/chequered plates), fiberglass reinforced plastic (grating, pultrusion) and electrical components (CT/PTs, feeder pillars), serving DISCOMs, government distribution schemes and private industrial/power-sector clients.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Raw materials (SMC, FRP, copper, mild steel, stainless steel; for FRP specifically glass fibre, additives and resin) are received from suppliers and subjected to receiving inspection, controlled-temperature storage and in-house laboratory testing before entering production. The Company is integrated into the intermediate stage of its own SMC value chain - it prepares the SMC compound in-house on a compounding machine (800 mm width, Ahmedabad) and matures it under controlled temperature before compression moulding, and it also sells that compound externally (11.08% of FY25 revenue from operations). It operates in-house testing laboratories at every stage (raw material, in-process, moulded-part, final and pre-dispatch inspection), but the text does not describe backward integration into resin or glass-fibre production. Forward integration extends to in-house post-moulding fabrication, assembly, packing, pre-dispatch inspection and dispatch/logistics directly to customers or project sites. The Company does not enter into long-term supply agreements with suppliers and purchases raw materials on a need basis, primarily through the spot-market purchase mechanism, seeking to source from diverse suppliers.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- FY25 revenue growth was driven by increased installed capacity, participation in government distribution schemes (SMNP, RDSS) and large private-sector orders for SMC boxes meeting required standards
- High customer concentration is an operating characteristic - Top 5 customers were 78.08% of revenue in H1FY26 (ranged 47.66%-76.81% over FY23-FY25)
- Debt-equity ratio has fallen sharply from 8.90x (FY23) to around 1.0x (FY24 through H1FY26), indicating deleveraging alongside the scale-up in revenue
- Geographic revenue mix shifted materially between periods - Gujarat was 64.30% of FY25 revenue versus …

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: Company undertook capital expenditure and expanded installed capacities across all segments in Fiscal 2025 versus Fiscal 2024, with capacity up 117.20% in the SMC segment and 74.71% in the FRP segment. During FY2025 it also established a new LTCT and CT/PT manufacturing unit at Nashik, Maharashtra, and introduced new products (FRP gratings, CT/PT units) based on confirmed business leads from power and transformer sector clients. The company currently operates four manufacturing facilities located across Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Diverse product range across SMC, FRP and CT/PT segments broadens client base across sectors and mitigates single-segment market risk
- Strong in-house manufacturing capabilities with advanced SMC/FRP production machinery enabling consistent quality and scale for large-volume orders

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Addresses in the Factory License, Consents to Establish/Operate and Lease Deeds for the Pirana, Ahmedabad facility do not match after the underlying land parcel was subdivided into two industrial parks in 2024, which could have legal implications for operations at that site
- Top 5 customers were 78.08% of revenue in H1FY26 (47.66%-76.81% across FY23-FY25), exposing revenue to the loss of a small number of large customers
- Maharashtra and Gujarat together accounted for over 90% of revenue in H1FY26, with the state-wise mix also swinging sharply between fiscal years
- Debt-equity ratio was as high as 8.90x in FY23, moderating to ~1.0x by FY24-H1FY26, reflecting a capital structure that was highly leveraged while the business was scaling
- A substantial part of FY25 revenue growth is linked to participation in government programs (SMNP, RDSS); a slowdown or change in these programs could affect order inflows
- Promoters (notably Nitin J. Patel) hold directorships/interests in multiple other group entities spanning pharmaceuticals, valves and engineering, which could divert management attention or create related-party dependencies
